## 10. Non-Functional Requirements

### 10.1 Security & audit
- NFR1 Independent security audit of all RoughNet proprietary contracts before mainnet/sidechain
  launch; re-audit on upgrade.
- NFR2 Reuse battle-tested OpenZeppelin / ERC-3643 libraries; minimize bespoke surface.
- NFR3 Atomicity for every value-moving operation (subscription, DvP, governance, migration,
  distribution) — no partial/limbo states.

### 10.2 Key management & privileged authority
- NFR4 Privileged roles (forced transfer, whitelist revocation, migration trigger, contract
  upgrade) governed by an **m-of-n Safe multisig** distributed across RoughNet, Ctrl Alt and a
  third-party trustee — no single "god-mode" key.
- NFR5 Master/operational key separation; offline storage for the highest-authority keys.
- NFR6 Embedded-wallet recovery must not require exposing or reconstructing seed phrases.

### 10.3 Compliance & privacy
- NFR7 No transfer executes outside the whitelist/claims rules (enforced on-chain).
- NFR8 Real-world identities never on-chain; only pseudonymous addresses + hashed document
  references. Sensitive documents off-chain (IPFS if public; permissioned store otherwise).
- NFR9 Immutable, hash-anchored provenance for Specifications, valuations, attestations, agreements.
- NFR10 Full regulatory-constraint catalogue enforced per transaction (working paper OI-8).

# RoughNet — Business & Product Requirements Document (BRD v2)

**Project:** RoughNet Tokenized Rough-Diamond Platform
**Version:** 2.0
**Date:** 2026-06-21
**Author:** RoughNet (drafted with Claude Opus 4.8)
**Status:** Draft for review

---

## 0. Document Control

### 0.1 Purpose
This document specifies **everything that must be built** to deliver the RoughNet platform —
smart contracts, web frontend, supporting services and integrations — and explicitly labels the
pieces that **must be provided by Ctrl Alt (the Issuer)** for the integration to work. It is a
business/product requirements document. *How* RoughNet will build it (Solidity architecture, repo
structure, audit plan, sprint plan) belongs in a separate technical design document.

### 0.2 Source hierarchy
| Source | Authority |
|---|---|
| `Tokenization of Rough Diamonds — v5 — Sven 6 May 2026.txt` (Tim Goodman) | **Leading** for all business process, roles, instruments and deal lifecycle. |
| `RoughNet_Gemini_2026-06-21_030736.md` | Leading for the RoughNet ↔ Ctrl Alt collaboration model and architecture decisions. |
| `RoughNet-BRD-v1-Gemini` | **Superseded / ignored.** Initial derived draft only. |
| `CONTEXT.md` (this repo) | Canonical glossary (ubiquitous language). |
| `docs/adr/0001..0004` | Binding architectural decisions. |

### 0.3 Key decisions baked into this BRD (see ADRs)
- **ADR-0001** — Individual on-chain custody; the cap table *is* the chain (no omnibus wallet).
- **ADR-0002** — ERC-3643 as the open-source compliance base; RoughNet writes only proprietary
  lifecycle + governance logic on top; Ctrl Alt operates the Identity Registry.
- **ADR-0003** — Chain-agnostic EVM; XRPL EVM Sidechain first; Ethereum mainnet a future option;
  bridging avoided.
- **ADR-0004** — Atomic stablecoin DvP default with off-chain fiat fallback; investors may choose
  embedded / self-custody / Issuer-custodial wallets.

### 0.4 Terminology note
"**R1 / Release 1**" denotes first-delivery scope. ("v1/v2" refer only to *document* versions.)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

RoughNet enables the **fractionalization of equity and/or debt in high-value rough diamond
"Specials"**, administered end-to-end by smart contracts on a regulator-approved EVM chain. A
Vendor with good title to a rough stone places it under an SPV cell, raises capital from
Subscribers by selling Fraction Tokens (equity) or Convertible Fractions (debt), and is
contractually required to retain a stake until the stone is polished. As the rough is manufactured
into one or more polished stones (the **Yield**), the platform performs an on-chain **burn-and-mint
migration** that converts each holder's rough fraction into pro-rata fractions of every resulting
polished stone, after which each stone can be liquidated independently. **Tag-Along, Drag-Along and
Shotgun** clauses are enforced natively on-chain, and all activity is published to a public,
API-exposed **Register**.

**Primary objective:** improve access to finance and liquidity for the rough-diamond trade.
**Secondary objective:** give Subscribers exposure to the rough-to-polished value upside.

**Division of labour:**
- **RoughNet** — Technology + co-Facilitator: all smart contracts (proprietary lifecycle &
  governance on an ERC-3643 base), the full web frontend (investor modules + internal consoles),
  the Register, physical sourcing/vaulting, and Audit Director coordination.
- **Ctrl Alt** — Issuer: VARA/DMCC licensing & legal issuance, KYC/AML and ONCHAINID claim
  issuance, the white-label investor-portal shell, fiat banking rails, and stablecoin
  mint/redeem + on/off-ramp.
- **Independent third parties** — Valuer (DMCC-licensed valuations), Audit Director
  (manufacturing attestations), Insurer, manufacturing partners.

---

## 2. Business Context & Objectives

### 2.1 Market rationale
Rough "Specials" carry genuine speculative upside (a well-planned cut typically yields polished
stones worth more than the rough) with a smaller downside if manufacturing goes wrong — unlike
polished diamonds, whose values are currently declining. The rough trade is financed today by an
informal, handshake syndication system and a narrow cohort of conservative banks, leaving the
market illiquid, gated by capital, and demographically stagnant.

### 2.2 Objectives
1. **O1 — Finance & liquidity (primary):** Replace informal syndication with a legally structured,
   transparently registered, more liquid framework; broaden the capital pool to trade participants
   and qualified external investors.
2. **O2 — Investor upside (secondary):** Provide fractional, tradable exposure to the
   rough-to-polished upside, priced at a discount to projected polished NAV.
3. **O3 — Compliance by construction:** Operate within VARA (ARVA) and DMCC frameworks with KYC/AML
   enforced on-chain, immutable provenance, and an auditable public Register.
4. **O4 — Lean RoughNet footprint:** RoughNet builds the Technology and runs the physical/Facilitator
   role; Ctrl Alt absorbs licensing, banking and compliance operations.
5. **O5 — Extensibility:** The same framework must later extend to other luxury RWAs (watches) and
   to insurance underwriting fractionalization (noted in the MOU purpose).

### 2.3 Non-goals (R1)
- Not a general crypto exchange or DeFi protocol.
- Not a custodian/bank — fiat custody, KYC and licensing are the Issuer's.
- Not multi-chain at launch (single EVM deployment; per-asset Ethereum optional later).

---

## 3. Actors & Roles

| Actor | Real entity | Platform-facing surface |
|---|---|---|
| **Subscriber** (investor; retail & institutional) | External | Investor portal (within Ctrl Alt shell) |
| **Vendor / Applicant** | Diamond owner | Vendor/Applicant console |
| **Facilitator / RoughNet Admin** | RoughNet | Facilitator console |
| **Issuer / Compliance Admin** | Ctrl Alt | Issuer services + KYC/claims back office |
| **Valuer** | Independent (DMCC-licensed) | Valuer input module |
| **Audit Director** | Independent (VARA/DMCC-approved) | Audit Director console |
| **Insurer / Loss adjuster** | Independent | Document submission (off-platform R1) |
| **Public / Regulator** | VARA, DMCC, public | Public Register (read-only API + UI) |

On-chain **roles** (access control): `FACILITATOR_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_AGENT` (ERC-3643 agent /
forced-transfer authority), `VALUER`, `AUDIT_DIRECTOR`, `SUBSCRIBER`. Privileged roles
(forced transfer, whitelist revocation, contract upgrade, migration trigger) are held by an
**m-of-n multisig (Safe)** distributed across RoughNet, Ctrl Alt and a third-party trustee — see
§10.2.

---

## 4. Scope & Phasing

### 4.1 Release 1 (build now)
- **SPV Type E — equity** fractionalization end-to-end.
- Onboarding/whitelisting (ERC-3643 + ONCHAINID), application → DD → valuation → cell creation.
- Diamond Token mint, Fraction Token issuance, primary subscription via **atomic stablecoin DvP**.
- Manufacturing oversight + Audit Director on-chain attestations; inclusion-fingerprint anchoring.
- **Rough → Polished migration** (burn-and-mint, pro-rata distribution).
- **Governance:** Shotgun, Drag-Along, Tag-Along.
- **Secondary transfers** (compliant peer-to-peer / DvP swaps) and **Yield distribution**.
- **Public Register** (API + read-only UI).
- Investor modules (embedded in Ctrl Alt shell) + Facilitator / Valuer / Audit Director consoles.

### 4.2 Release 2 (specified now, built later)
- **SPV Type D — debt:** Convertible Notes / CTN, Convertible Fractions, interest accrual
  (capitalized vs liquidity-buffer, per-deal), conversion-to-equity and early-settlement/buy-back,
  anti-double-pledge encumbrance register.
- Full standalone RoughNet platform (graduating out of Ctrl Alt's shell — see §8.1).
- Integrated secondary order book / matching.

### 4.3 Candidate / decision-pending scope
- **Acquisition financing** (a buyer raises capital to *acquire* a not-yet-owned rough; SPV takes
  title on settlement). Default R1 model is **sell-down/finance of already-owned stones** (working
  paper). Both paths are documented (§5.2) and the choice is an **open decision (OI-1)**.
- Fraction Tokens as collateral for secondary financing ("needs further consideration" — working
  paper def. 14).
- Extension to watches / insurance underwriting (O5).

---

## 5. End-to-End Deal Lifecycle

### 5.1 Primary path — equity sell-down (R1 default)
1. **Application.** Vendor with good title applies to fractionalize a rough.
2. **Due diligence.** Issuer (Ctrl Alt) completes KYC/AML on the Applicant and title DD; on pass,
   the Applicant's wallet is added to the on-chain allow-list.
3. **Acceptance in principle**, subject to valuation.
4. **Valuation.** Independent Valuer inspects and values the rough and projected Yield (dual
   valuations — OI-7).
5. **Cell creation.** A dedicated SPV Type E cell is opened; Stakeholder's Agreement generated from
   template; specie + PI insurance certificate obtained.
6. **Diamond Token mint.** Digital twin minted with Specifications + inclusion fingerprint anchored
   immutably.
7. **Fraction issuance.** Cell issues shares → tokenized into Fraction Tokens (ERC-3643) by the
   Issuer. Vendor retains mandatory equity.
8. **Primary subscription.** Subscribers buy Fraction Tokens at a discount to projected polished
   NAV via **atomic stablecoin DvP**; proceeds released to the Vendor; SPV holds 100% legal custody.
9. **Manufacturing.** Stone moves only to vetted/bonded manufacturers under Audit Director
   supervision; attestations written on-chain per cut stage.
10. **Migration.** Rough Token series burned; per-polished-stone Fraction Token series minted
    pro-rata to all rough holders.
11. **Independent liquidity.** Holders trade or liquidate per-stone; governance clauses apply.
12. **Yield distribution.** On sale of a polished stone, proceeds distribute immediately to that
    stone's series holders per the encoded rules.

### 5.2 Alternative entry — acquisition financing (decision-pending, OI-1)
A prospective buyer raises a Convertible Note from Subscribers; escrowed proceeds fund the purchase;
SPV takes title on settlement and the buyer becomes the Vendor. Requires escrow-to-purchase and
failed-purchase refund flows. Naturally aligns with the **debt path (R2)**.

### 5.3 Debt path — Convertible Notes (R2)
Same governance and workflow as equity, but the cell issues a Convertible Note → tokenized →
fractionalized into Convertible Fractions. Adds interest (periodic or capitalized), conversion
rights, early settlement/buy-back, and Register encumbrance entries to prevent double-pledging.

---

## 6. Functional Requirements by Epic

Each epic lists **User Stories**, **Smart-Contract requirements [RoughNet]**, **Frontend
requirements [RoughNet]**, and **Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]**.

### Epic 1 — Identity, KYC & On-Chain Whitelisting
**User stories**
- As a Subscriber, I pass KYC once and can then transact 24/7 without per-trade approval.
- As an Issuer Compliance Admin, I can revoke a wallet instantly, blocking future transfers.
- As a Subscriber who lost my key, I can recover my identity to a new address without losing tokens.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR1.1 Integrate ERC-3643 token + Identity Registry + Compliance modules as the base layer.
- FR1.2 Enforce that all transfers (`transfer`, `transferFrom`, DvP, forced) revert unless both
  parties are whitelisted and claims are valid (not expired/revoked).
- FR1.3 Support identity recovery: rebind an ONCHAINID to a new address and re-point token balances
  without burning underlying Fraction Tokens.
- FR1.4 Support partial freeze of a wallet's balance (regulator hold) leaving the rest liquid.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR1.5 Wallet-type selector at onboarding: (a) embedded AA smart wallet (passkey + recovery,
  default for retail), (b) self-custody EOA, (c) Issuer custodial. Abstract wallet type across all
  flows.
- FR1.6 KYC status indicator and "what you can do" surface driven by live claim state.
- FR1.7 Recovery wizard for lost embedded-wallet keys.

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]**
- FR1.8 **[Ctrl Alt]** Perform KYC/AML and push cryptographically signed claims to each
  Subscriber's ONCHAINID (the claim-issuer service).
- FR1.9 **[Ctrl Alt]** Operate/own the Identity Registry deployment and trusted-claim-issuer keys.
- FR1.10 **[Ctrl Alt]** Provide the KYC document-capture wizard within the white-label shell.

### Epic 2 — Application, Due Diligence, Valuation & Cell Creation
**User stories**
- As a Vendor, I apply to fractionalize a stone and track my application status.
- As a Facilitator, I accept/reject applications and trigger valuation.
- As a Valuer, I record realizable valuations of the rough and projected Yield.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR2.1 Create an SPV cell record on-chain (deal id, SPV type, Stakeholder's Agreement hash,
  insurance certificate hash).
- FR2.2 Store Valuer attestations (rough valuation, projected Yield valuation) with Valuer
  signature; support dual valuations.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR2.3 Vendor/Applicant console: application form, document upload (title, KP, scans), status
  tracker.
- FR2.4 Facilitator console: application queue, accept/reject with reasons, valuation

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]**

### Epic 3 — Diamond Token & Fraction Token Issuance
**User stories**
- As a Facilitator, I mint the Diamond Token (digital twin) with immutable Specifications.
- As an Issuer, I issue the Fraction Tokens for the cell.
- As a Vendor, I retain mandatory equity that I cannot release until polishing is signed off.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR3.1 Mint a Diamond Token binding Specifications + inclusion-fingerprint hash + document hashes
  (IPFS/permissioned URIs), immutable.
- FR3.2 Issue an ERC-3643 Fraction Token series for the cell with a fixed total supply.
- FR3.3 Enforce **Vendor lock-up**: the Vendor's mandatory retained fractions cannot transfer until
  the Audit Director signs off polishing completion.
- FR3.4 Bind each Fraction Token series to its Diamond Token and Stakeholder's Agreement.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR3.5 Facilitator issuance wizard with pre-mint validation (sum of allocations, retention,
  discount, metadata completeness).
- FR3.6 Investor: Diamond Token detail page (Specifications, scans, GIA/Galaxy/KP, valuation,
  insurance, document hashes with verify links).

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]**
- FR3.7 **[Ctrl Alt]** Legal authority to issue (VARA Issuer license) and the ERC-3643 token

### Epic 4 — Primary Subscription & Settlement (Treasury / DvP)
**User stories**
- As a Subscriber, I buy Fraction Tokens with stablecoin and receive them atomically.
- As an institutional Subscriber, I may settle a large ticket by fiat wire with reconciliation.
- As a Vendor, I receive subscription proceeds on completion.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR4.1 Atomic **DvP**: stablecoin payment and Fraction Token delivery swap or revert together.
- FR4.2 Escrow stablecoin for pending/conditional flows (and governance windows — see Epic 7).
- FR4.3 Emit settlement events (subscription, release-to-Vendor) consumable by the Issuer's banking
  reconciliation for the fiat fallback path.
- FR4.4 Configurable primary-offering parameters per cell (price/discount, caps, per-investor
  limits, optional funding target/deadline if acquisition-financing OI-1 is enabled).

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR4.5 Subscription flow: amount, live price/discount, fees, stablecoin balance, DvP confirmation;
  fiat-wire instructions + status for the fallback path.

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]**
- FR4.7 **[Ctrl Alt]** Stablecoin mint/redeem + fiat **on/off-ramp** (AED/USD ⇄ stablecoin).
- FR4.8 **[Ctrl Alt]** Regulated escrow bank accounts and the fiat settlement leg for the fallback.
- FR4.9 **[Ctrl Alt]** Reconciliation webhooks listening to RoughNet settlement events.

### Epic 5 — Manufacturing Oversight & Oracle (Physical ↔ Digital Integrity)
**User stories**
- As an Audit Director, I attest to each cut stage on-chain so investors trust the Yield is the
  original stone.
- As a Subscriber, I can see verified manufacturing milestones.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR5.1 Store Audit Director attestations against the Diamond Token at each cut stage (stage id,
  intermediate scan/fingerprint hash, signature, timestamp).
- FR5.2 Gate the migration (Epic 6) on a final Audit Director "polishing complete" attestation.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR5.3 Audit Director console: cut-plan view, per-stage attestation submission, intermediate scan

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]** — none (independent Audit Director; Ctrl Alt has no role).

### Epic 6 — Rough → Polished Migration (Burn-and-Mint)
**User stories**
- As a Facilitator, I execute migration so each rough holder receives pro-rata shares of every
  polished stone.
- As a Subscriber, my dashboard automatically reflects my new per-stone holdings.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR6.1 Snapshot rough-series holders at migration.
- FR6.2 Burn the rough series; for each polished stone mint a new ERC-3643 Fraction Token series.
- FR6.3 Distribute each new series pro-rata to the snapshot (10% of rough → 10% of each stone),
  preserving whitelisting and lock-ups.
- FR6.4 Bind each new series to its own polished Diamond Token + metadata (per-stone GIA, scan).

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR6.6 Facilitator migration wizard: define N polished stones, per-stone metadata, preview
  distribution, execute.
- FR6.7 Investor: asset-split history tracing current per-stone fractions back to the original

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]** — ERC-3643 issuance authority for each new series.

### Epic 7 — Corporate Governance (Shotgun, Drag-Along, Tag-Along)
**User stories**
- As any holder, I can trigger a **Shotgun**: name a price, the counterparty must buy or sell within
  48h.
- As a selling Party with a 100% buyer, I can **Drag-Along** the others on the same terms (subject
  first to Shotgun).
- As a non-selling Party, I can **Tag-Along** into a sale on the same terms (subject first to

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR7.1 Shotgun: offeror names price/quantity & target; escrow the offeror's stablecoin/tokens;

  price/terms; auto-execute the default outcome on expiry.
- FR7.2 Drag-Along: a qualifying seller compels remaining holders to sell at agreed terms via
  ERC-3643 forced transfer, with the cash leg settled atomically to each dragged holder.
- FR7.3 Tag-Along: notify eligible holders of a pending qualifying sale; allow opt-in to sell pro-rata

- FR7.4 Enforce clause ordering: Drag/Tag are **subject first to the Shotgun**.
- FR7.5 Per-cell configurable triggers, thresholds and voting weights (OI-1 of the working paper).

**Frontend [RoughNet]** — *the Governance Hub, RoughNet's signature module*

  to (e.g. hide Drag-Along unless thresholds met) to avoid wasted gas and generic reverts.
- FR7.8 Shotgun module: price-per-fraction + target selector + escrow preview + "Initiate".
- FR7.9 Tag-Along panel: pending qualifying sales + "Opt-in to sell".
- FR7.10 Drag-Along flow: initiate, show affected holders, settlement preview.
- FR7.11 Active-events dashboard with countdown timers and required actions.

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]**
- FR7.12 **[Ctrl Alt]** Fiat leg for any forced sale settling off-chain (fallback path), triggered
  by emitted governance events.

- As a holder, I can sell a per-stone fraction to another whitelisted investor.
- As a holder, I cannot accidentally trade in violation of the rules.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR8.1 Compliant peer-to-peer **DvP swap** contract (token ⇄ stablecoin, both sides whitelisted,
  atomic).
- FR8.2 `canTransfer`-style pre-check function the UI can call to grey out invalid actions.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR8.3 Per-stone listing/offer UI with soft constraints; clear "why this is blocked" messaging.
- FR8.4 (R2) Order book / matching, or integration with an ERC-3643-aware ATS.

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]** — stablecoin rail + (optional) regulated ATS venue.

### Epic 9 — Yield Distribution
**User stories**
- As a holder of a polished stone's series, I receive my pro-rata proceeds immediately on its sale.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR9.1 On sale of a polished stone, distribute proceeds (stablecoin) pro-rata to that series'
  holders atomically; handle the Vendor's retained share and any debt waterfall (R2).
- FR9.2 Optionally retire/burn the sold stone's series on full exit.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR9.3 Distribution statements and claimable-proceeds view.

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]** — fiat payout for off-chain settlement; tax/withholding handling.

### Epic 10 — Public Register & Reporting
**User stories**
- As the public/a regulator, I can inspect Diamond Tokens, Fraction Tokens, Notes and encumbrances
  via a human-readable, API-exposed Register.
- As a regulator, I can verify scarcity and the ownership-change audit trail without seeing private
  identities.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR10.1 Emit a complete, indexable event trail for all lifecycle and governance actions.

**Frontend / Services [RoughNet]**
- FR10.2 Public Register: read-only UI + documented public API (Diamond Tokens, series, supply,
  ownership-change trail, encumbrances) in human-readable form.
- FR10.3 Configurable public-vs-whitelisted-only data surface (per VARA — OI-6).

**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]** — agreement on the public/private data boundary with VARA.

### Epic 11 — Debt / Convertible Notes (R2 — specified now)
**User stories**
- As a Vendor, I raise debt against my stone and retain possession during polishing under the Terms.
- As a Subscriber, I hold Convertible Fractions earning interest and/or convert to equity.

**Smart-contract [RoughNet]**
- FR11.1 Convertible Note (CTN) instrument + Convertible Fraction tokenization.
- FR11.2 Interest accrual: capitalized vs liquidity-buffer, per-deal election (OI-2).
- FR11.3 Conversion-to-equity and early-settlement/buy-back options under the Terms.
- FR11.4 **Encumbrance register** preventing double-pledging of the same collateral.

**Frontend [RoughNet]** — debt subscription, interest/coupon view, conversion controls,
encumbrance display.
**Issuer dependencies [Ctrl Alt]** — debt-issuance licensing, interest payment rails.

### Epic 12 — Facilitator & Operations Consoles
**User stories**
- As a Facilitator, I manage deals, cells, roles, and trigger privileged actions through the
  multisig.
- As an admin, I monitor system state, attestations and settlement health.

**Frontend [RoughNet]**
- FR12.1 Facilitator console: deal/cell lifecycle management, role assignment, multisig-backed
  privileged actions (migration, forced transfer, whitelist revocation, upgrades), audit log.
- FR12.2 Operational dashboards: pending KYC, valuations, attestations, settlements, governance

---

## 7. Frontend Functionality Catalogue (RoughNet)

shell** (login, KYC wizard, fiat dashboards = Ctrl Alt). Internal consoles are standalone RoughNet

- Notifications (governance deadlines, attestations, settlement).

**B. Vendor / Applicant console** — application, document upload, status, retained-equity view,
release controls (post-sign-off).

**C. Facilitator / Admin console** — application queue, cell creation/issuance, migration wizard,
role & multisig actions, operational dashboards, audit log.

**D. Valuer module** — structured, signed valuation entry & history.

**E. Audit Director console** — cut-plan, per-stage attestation, scan upload, polishing sign-off.

**F. Public Register UI** — read-only explorer over the public API.

---

## 8. Architecture & Integration Constraints (business-level)

### 8.1 Frontend ownership (R1 → future)
- **R1:** RoughNet builds the custom lifecycle/governance modules embedded in **Ctrl Alt's
  white-label shell**; modules must be portable (clean API boundary, no hard coupling to the shell).
- **Future:** RoughNet may graduate to a **fully standalone platform** consuming Ctrl Alt as
  headless services (KYC/claims, fiat ramp, stablecoin). Architect for this from day one.

### 8.2 Chain
Chain-agnostic EVM; **XRPL EVM Sidechain** first if required for Ctrl Alt compliance/support;
**Ethereum mainnet** an option for selected stones / future releases when Subscribers want direct
stablecoin investment; bridging avoided (ADR-0003).

### 8.3 Compliance base
ERC-3643 + ONCHAINID; Issuer operates the Identity Registry and claim issuance; RoughNet writes only
proprietary logic on top (ADR-0002).

### 8.4 Settlement & custody
Atomic stablecoin DvP default + off-chain fiat fallback; investor-selectable wallet custody
(ADR-0004).

---

## 9. Responsibility Matrix

| Capability | RoughNet | Ctrl Alt (Issuer) | Independent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Physical sourcing, vaulting, logistics | ● | | |
| Smart contracts (lifecycle, governance, migration, DvP) | ● | | |
| ERC-3643 base integration | ● | (template/agent config) | |
| Identity Registry + KYC claim issuance | | ● | |
| KYC/AML, title DD, legal issuance, VARA/DMCC licensing | | ● | |
| Fiat banking rails, escrow, on/off-ramp, stablecoin mint/redeem | | ● | |
| White-label investor-portal shell (login/KYC/fiat dashboards) | (embed modules) | ● | |
| Investor lifecycle/governance UI modules | ● | | |
| Facilitator / Valuer / Audit Director consoles | ● | | |
| Public Register (contracts, API, UI) | ● | (data-boundary sign-off) | |
| Valuation | | | ● Valuer |
| Manufacturing attestations / oracle | ● (coordination) | | ● Audit Director |
| Insurance (specie + PI) | (arrange) | | ● Insurer |

---

## 10. Non-Functional Requirements

### 10.1 Security & audit
- NFR1 Independent security audit of all RoughNet proprietary contracts before mainnet/sidechain
  launch; re-audit on upgrade.
- NFR2 Reuse battle-tested OpenZeppelin / ERC-3643 libraries; minimize bespoke surface.
- NFR3 Atomicity for every value-moving operation (subscription, DvP, governance, migration,
  distribution) — no partial/limbo states.

### 10.2 Key management & privileged authority
- NFR4 Privileged roles (forced transfer, whitelist revocation, migration trigger, contract
  upgrade) governed by an **m-of-n Safe multisig** distributed across RoughNet, Ctrl Alt and a
  third-party trustee — no single "god-mode" key.
- NFR5 Master/operational key separation; offline storage for the highest-authority keys.
- NFR6 Embedded-wallet recovery must not require exposing or reconstructing seed phrases.

### 10.3 Compliance & privacy
- NFR7 No transfer executes outside the whitelist/claims rules (enforced on-chain).
- NFR8 Real-world identities never on-chain; only pseudonymous addresses + hashed document
  references. Sensitive documents off-chain (IPFS if public; permissioned store otherwise).
- NFR9 Immutable, hash-anchored provenance for Specifications, valuations, attestations, agreements.
- NFR10 Full regulatory-constraint catalogue enforced per transaction (working paper OI-8).

### 10.4 Availability, performance, UX
- NFR11 24/7 compliant trading with no human-in-the-loop per trade.
- NFR12 Soft-constraint UI everywhere a hard on-chain revert is possible.
- NFR13 Retail-grade onboarding (no crypto literacy assumed) via embedded wallets.
- NFR14 Deterministic, low, predictable fees suitable for both whale and (future) retail tickets.

### 10.5 Extensibility
- NFR15 Asset-type-agnostic core (diamonds R1; watches / insurance underwriting later — O5).

---

## 11. Open Items & Decisions Pending

| ID | Item | Owner | Default / lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | Acquisition financing vs sell-down-only for R1 | RoughNet + Ctrl Alt | Sell-down only (R1); acquisition via debt later |
| OI-2 | Debt interest formula (capitalized vs liquidity-buffer, or per-deal) | Facilitator | Per-deal election (R2) |
| OI-3 | Smart-contract authorship/upgrade control (Facilitator/Issuer/joint) | Both | RoughNet authors; multisig upgrade control (§10.2) |
| OI-4 | Migration spec + Audit Director attestation format | RoughNet | Finalize in technical design |
| OI-5 | Inclusion-fingerprint standard + polished-out edge cases | RoughNet + DMCC/VARA | Sarine/Galaxy-based; research edge cases |
| OI-6 | Register public-vs-whitelisted data surface | Ctrl Alt + VARA | Public scarcity/ownership trail; private identities |
| OI-7 | Valuer panel (dual valuations) | Facilitator | E-valuer + one more DMCC valuer |
| OI-8 | Full regulatory-constraint catalogue enforced per tx | Ctrl Alt | Compile with VARA |
| OI-9 | Shotgun trigger thresholds & voting weights | Facilitator | Per-cell configurable |
| OI-10 | Fraction Tokens as collateral for secondary financing | RoughNet | Deferred |

---

## 12. Consolidated Ctrl Alt (Issuer) Deliverables — handoff list

1. VARA/DMCC Issuer licensing & legal token issuance authority (ARVA framework).
2. KYC/AML + title due-diligence operations and sign-off.
3. **ONCHAINID Identity Registry** deployment + signed-claim issuance service + trusted-issuer keys.
4. ERC-3643 base token template / agent-role configuration aligned to RoughNet's interfaces.
5. Fiat banking rails: regulated escrow accounts, on/off-ramp (AED/USD ⇄ stablecoin), stablecoin
   mint/redeem.
6. Reconciliation webhooks consuming RoughNet settlement & governance events (fiat fallback path).
7. White-label investor-portal shell (login, KYC wizard, fiat dashboards) hosting RoughNet's modules.
8. Agreement with VARA on the Register's public-vs-private data boundary.
9. (R2) Debt-issuance licensing and interest payment rails.

---

See `CONTEXT.md` (canonical ubiquitous language). Architectural rationale in `docs/adr/`.

## What I delivered

**`docs-dev/RoughNet-BRD-v2-Opus4.8.md`** — a comprehensive BRD built on the v5 working paper as the leading source (BRD-v1 ignored as you instructed). It covers: executive summary, business objectives, the full actor/role model, scope & phasing, the end-to-end deal lifecycle, **12 epics** (each with user stories + smart-contract reqs + frontend reqs + explicitly-labeled Ctrl Alt dependencies), a detailed **frontend functionality catalogue**, a responsibility matrix, non-functional/security requirements, a consolidated **Ctrl Alt handoff list**, and 10 tracked open items.

## The decisions we resolved by grilling

The doc you handed me contained a load-bearing contradiction (omnibus wallet vs. on-chain governance) that v1 papered over. We settled the whole design tree:

1. **Custody** → individual on-chain wallets; cap table *is* the chain (keeps your Solidity governance meaningful).
2. **Chain** → chain-agnostic EVM, XRPL EVM Sidechain first, Ethereum optional later.
3. **Entity mapping** → RoughNet = Tech + co-Facilitator; Ctrl Alt = Issuer; Valuer/Audit Director independent.
4. **Deal entry** → owner sell-down (working-paper default); acquisition-financing documented as a pending decision.
5. **Settlement** → atomic stablecoin DvP default + fiat fallback.
6. **Scope** → Equity (Type E) in R1; Debt/CTN (Type D) specified now, built R2.
7. **Frontend** → RoughNet modules embedded in Ctrl Alt's shell, built portably to go standalone later.
8. **Wallets** → investor's choice of embedded / self-custody / custodial.

## Worth flagging
- The "how we build it" technical design (Solidity architecture, audit plan, sprint breakdown) is deliberately *not* here — you said it becomes one or two separate documents. The BRD points to it but stops at the requirements boundary.
- **OI-1** (acquisition financing vs. sell-down-only) and **OI-3** (contract authorship/upgrade control) are the two open items most likely to affect the MOU language with Ctrl Alt — you may want to close those before the BRD goes external.

# To Issues

Break a plan into independently-grabbable issues using vertical slices (tracer bullets).

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes an issue reference (issue number, URL, or path) as an argument, fetch it from the issue tracker and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Issue titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the plan into **tracer bullet** issues. Each issue is a thin vertical slice that cuts through ALL integration layers end-to-end, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice delivers a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests)
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each slice, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other slices (if any) must complete first
- **User stories covered**: which user stories this addresses (if the source material has them)

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the dependency relationships correct?
- Should any slices be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the issues to the issue tracker

For each approved slice, publish a new issue to the issue tracker. Use the issue body template below. These issues are considered ready for AFK agents, so publish them with the correct triage label unless instructed otherwise.

Publish issues in dependency order (blockers first) so you can reference real issue identifiers in the "Blocked by" field.

<issue-template>
## Parent

A reference to the parent issue on the issue tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

## What to build

A concise description of this vertical slice. Describe the end-to-end behavior, not layer-by-layer implementation.

Avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it here and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2
- [ ] Criterion 3

## Blocked by

- A reference to the blocking ticket (if any)

Or "None - can start immediately" if no blockers.

</issue-template>

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

## Proposed vertical slices (R1 = equity / SPV Type E)

Each is a thin end-to-end tracer bullet (contracts + UI + tests), demoable on its own. Debt/CTN (Epic 11), standalone-platform graduation, and real Ctrl Alt integration are explicitly out of this R1 set.

**0. Walking skeleton & toolchain** *(prefactor)*
Monorepo, EVM toolchain (contracts + deploy scripts), frontend app skeleton embeddable as a module, CI, local/testnet deploy. Tracer: deploy a trivial contract, read its state in the UI.
- Blocked by: None.
- Stories: enabler.

**1. Identity, KYC claim & on-chain whitelist**
Integrate ERC-3643 base + ONCHAINID with a **mock claim-issuer**. Onboard a wallet (wallet-type selector stub), show KYC status; a whitelisted transfer succeeds, a non-whitelisted one reverts. Includes instant revocation.
- Blocked by: 0.
- Stories: Epic 1 (FR1.1–1.10).

**2. Cell creation + Diamond Token & Fraction Token issuance**
Facilitator console wizard: create an SPV cell (agreement/insurance hashes), mint a Diamond Token with Specifications + inclusion-fingerprint hash, issue a Fraction Token series with Vendor mandatory-retention lock-up. Investor sees the Diamond detail page + (zero) balance.
- Blocked by: 1.
- Stories: Epics 2 (min), 3.

**3. Primary subscription via atomic stablecoin DvP**
Subscriber buys fractions atomically against a **mock stablecoin** (token + cash swap or revert together); portfolio + proceeds-to-Vendor update; settlement events emitted for later reconciliation.
- Blocked by: 2.
- Stories: Epic 4.

**4. Manufacturing attestations (Audit Director)**
Audit Director console: per-cut-stage on-chain attestations against the Diamond Token; final "polishing complete" sign-off that gates migration. Investor manufacturing timeline.
- Blocked by: 2.
- Stories: Epic 5.

**5. Rough → Polished migration (burn-and-mint)**
Gated by the final attestation: snapshot rough holders, burn rough series, mint a Fraction series per polished stone, distribute pro-rata atomically. Investor portfolio shows per-stone holdings + split lineage.
- Blocked by: 3, 4.
- Stories: Epic 6.

**6. Governance — Shotgun** *(signature module)*
Initiate Shotgun (named price + target + escrow + 48h timer); counterparty settles via DvP or exercises the reverse buy; deterministic default on expiry. Governance Hub UI with soft-constraint pre-validation + live timers.
- Blocked by: 5.
- Stories: Epic 7 (FR7.1, 7.6–7.9, 7.11).

**7. Governance — Drag-Along & Tag-Along**
Drag-Along forced transfer + Tag-Along opt-in, both **subject first to Shotgun**, with atomic cash legs. Extends the Governance Hub.
- Blocked by: 6.
- Stories: Epic 7 (FR7.2–7.5, 7.10, 7.12).

# QA Session

Run an interactive QA session. The user describes problems they're encountering. You clarify, explore the codebase for context, and file GitHub issues that are durable, user-focused, and use the project's domain language.

## For each issue the user raises

### 1. Listen and lightly clarify

Let the user describe the problem in their own words. Ask **at most 2-3 short clarifying questions** focused on:

- What they expected vs what actually happened
- Steps to reproduce (if not obvious)
- Whether it's consistent or intermittent

Do NOT over-interview. If the description is clear enough to file, move on.

### 2. Explore the codebase in the background

While talking to the user, kick off an Agent (subagent_type=Explore) in the background to understand the relevant area. The goal is NOT to find a fix — it's to:

- Learn the domain language used in that area (check UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md)
- Understand what the feature is supposed to do
- Identify the user-facing behavior boundary

This context helps you write a better issue — but the issue itself should NOT reference specific files, line numbers, or internal implementation details.

### 3. Assess scope: single issue or breakdown?

Before filing, decide whether this is a **single issue** or needs to be **broken down** into multiple issues.

Break down when:

- The fix spans multiple independent areas (e.g. "the form validation is wrong AND the success message is missing AND the redirect is broken")
- There are clearly separable concerns that different people could work on in parallel
- The user describes something that has multiple distinct failure modes or symptoms

Keep as a single issue when:

- It's one behavior that's wrong in one place
- The symptoms are all caused by the same root behavior

### 4. File the GitHub issue(s)

Create issues with `gh issue create`. Do NOT ask the user to review first — just file and share URLs.

Issues must be **durable** — they should still make sense after major refactors. Write from the user's perspective.

#### For a single issue

Use this template:

```
## What happened

[Describe the actual behavior the user experienced, in plain language]

## What I expected

[Describe the expected behavior]

## Steps to reproduce

1. [Concrete, numbered steps a developer can follow]
2. [Use domain terms from the codebase, not internal module names]
3. [Include relevant inputs, flags, or configuration]

## Additional context

[Any extra observations from the user or from codebase exploration that help frame the issue — e.g. "this only happens when using the Docker layer, not the filesystem layer" — use domain language but don't cite files]
```

#### For a breakdown (multiple issues)

Create issues in dependency order (blockers first) so you can reference real issue numbers.

Use this template for each sub-issue:

```
## Parent issue

#<parent-issue-number> (if you created a tracking issue) or "Reported during QA session"

## What's wrong

[Describe this specific behavior problem — just this slice, not the whole report]

## What I expected

[Expected behavior for this specific slice]

## Steps to reproduce

1. [Steps specific to THIS issue]

## Blocked by

- #<issue-number> (if this issue can't be fixed until another is resolved)

Or "None — can start immediately" if no blockers.

## Additional context

[Any extra observations relevant to this slice]
```

When creating a breakdown:

- **Prefer many thin issues over few thick ones** — each should be independently fixable and verifiable
- **Mark blocking relationships honestly** — if issue B genuinely can't be tested until issue A is fixed, say so. If they're independent, mark both as "None — can start immediately"
- **Create issues in dependency order** so you can reference real issue numbers in "Blocked by"
- **Maximize parallelism** — the goal is that multiple people (or agents) can grab different issues simultaneously

#### Rules for all issue bodies

- **No file paths or line numbers** — these go stale
- **Use the project's domain language** (check UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md if it exists)
- **Describe behaviors, not code** — "the sync service fails to apply the patch" not "applyPatch() throws on line 42"
- **Reproduction steps are mandatory** — if you can't determine them, ask the user
- **Keep it concise** — a developer should be able to read the issue in 30 seconds

After filing, print all issue URLs (with blocking relationships summarized) and ask: "Next issue, or are we done?"

### 5. Continue the session

Keep going until the user says they're done. Each issue is independent — don't batch them.

- newsjack-monitor-setup: Set up a newsjack monitoring profile for a company so newsjack-detector can run on a schedule. Never writes angles or pitches, and never drops a fresh big story. - Run as the standing-triage stage of the newsjack-detector pipeline, after the deterministic freshness gate (origin-apply) and before angle-generator. Uses calibrated anchors, hard anti-inflation rules, standing checks, timing windows, and brand-safety kill switches. - User asks if something is newsworthy, worth pitching, worth newsjacking, likely to get press, strong enough for journalists, or asks for a score/rubric/check on a current event, company announcement, pitch idea, or news hook.

- pr-strategist: Opinionated startup-PR strategist that helps founders figure out audience, positioning, news pegs, and drumbeat before any tactical PR. - qa: Interactive QA session where user reports bugs or issues conversationally, and the agent files GitHub issues. Explores the codebase in the background for context and domain language. Use when user wants to report bugs, do QA, file issues conversationally, or mentions "QA session".
